title: The Reviving Effect of Verses in the Age of Ignorance

questions.question: What does the passage ask you to imagine at the beginning?
questions.answer: A dark time of ignorance and rough living before the light of the Qur’an was seen clearly.

questions.question: In that imagined time, how were things around people covered?
questions.answer: They were covered by ignorance, heedlessness, and the idea that things were only lifeless nature.

questions.question: When the verses are heard, what happens to the creatures in the listeners’ minds?
questions.answer: They seem to come alive, wake up, and praise Allah.

questions.question: What do the stars become like in the picture given in the passage?
questions.answer: They become like bright words and lights showing wisdom.

questions.question: What does the earth become like in that picture?
questions.answer: It becomes like a head.

questions.question: What are the land and sea compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to tongues.

questions.question: What are animals and plants shown as doing?
questions.answer: They are shown glorifying Allah.

questions.question: Why might a person fail to feel the sweetness and wonder of these verses?
questions.answer: Because the person may be too used to hearing them and look at them only in a shallow way.

questions.question: What does the passage say each verse scatters?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: What does each verse spread instead?
questions.answer: Light, guidance, and miraculous beauty.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens over time to these verses in people’s minds?
questions.answer: People come to know them widely and accept them.

questions.question: If someone wants to understand one of the highest levels of the Qur’an’s miraculousness, what should that person do next?
questions.answer: Listen to the comparison that follows.

questions.question: What big job of the Qur’an is described in this passage?
questions.answer: It lights up darkness and guides people to belief.

questions.question: The passage compares the verses to what in the sky?
questions.answer: Shining stars.

questions.question: What kind of darkness do these shining verses remove?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: What kind of place and time are readers told to picture?
questions.answer: A harsh desert-like time of ignorance and savagery.

questions.question: Before the verses are heard, how do creatures seem to people?
questions.answer: They seem dead or asleep.

questions.question: After the verses are heard, how do those same creatures seem?
questions.answer: They seem awake, alive, and busy praising Allah.

questions.question: In the passage’s picture, what does the sky seem like?
questions.answer: A mouth.

questions.question: In the same picture, what do animals and plants seem like?
questions.answer: Words of glorification.

questions.question: Why does the passage tell readers to look from that old time instead of only from today?
questions.answer: So they can notice how much light and change the verses brought.

questions.question: What can make a person miss the special beauty of the verses?
questions.answer: Looking at them in a careless, overly familiar way.

questions.question: Besides miraculousness, what other light do the verses bring?
questions.answer: Guidance.

questions.question: What is the main feeling the passage wants the reader to have about the verses?
questions.answer: Wonder, thankfulness, and appreciation for Allah’s words.

questions.question: At the start, what are the Qur’an’s verses said to be like?
questions.answer: Bright stars.

questions.question: What do these bright stars do?
questions.answer: They spread light and push away darkness.

questions.question: What false way of seeing the world is shown in the dark old setting?
questions.answer: Thinking everything is only lifeless nature.

questions.question: When the verses are heard, what do listeners begin to understand about creation?
questions.answer: That creation is alive with signs and praises of Allah.

questions.question: What happens in the minds of the listeners when they hear the call to glorify Allah?
questions.answer: The world seems to wake up and remember Allah.

questions.question: How are the stars described after the verses are heard?
questions.answer: As meaningful lights that speak wisdom and truth.

questions.question: How is the earth described after the verses are heard?
questions.answer: As if it were a head with land and sea like tongues.

questions.question: What do all living things on earth become like in this picture?
questions.answer: Expressions of praise to Allah.

questions.question: Why is it hard for people today to fully notice what each verse changed?
questions.answer: Because the verses have been known for a long time, so people may not notice the first darkness they removed.

questions.question: What does “a veil of familiarity” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: Being so used to something that you stop noticing how amazing it is.

questions.question: What two things shine from the verses in this passage?
questions.answer: Miraculousness and guidance.

questions.question: What does the passage invite the reader to do after this explanation?
questions.answer: To listen to a comparison that explains the Qur’an’s greatness even more.

questions.question: What does the passage want you to appreciate about each verse of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: That each one gives light and drives away disbelief.

questions.question: In the first picture, what kind of age are we asked to imagine?
questions.answer: A time filled with ignorance and roughness.

questions.question: In that time, how did people wrongly view the world around them?
questions.answer: As dull, lifeless, and only natural.

questions.question: What change happens when Qur’anic words are heard?
questions.answer: The world is seen as living and praising Allah.

questions.question: Who seems to wake up when the verses are heard?
questions.answer: The creatures of the world.

questions.question: What do the stars look like to the listeners in this new view?
questions.answer: Like lights that speak truth and show wisdom.

questions.question: What do the land and sea look like in this new view?
questions.answer: Like tongues on the earth.

questions.question: What lesson does this picture teach about animals and plants?
questions.answer: They also show praise and signs of Allah.

questions.question: Why is just a quick and simple look not enough?
questions.answer: Because it hides the deep beauty and wonder of the verses.

questions.question: What has happened to these verses over time?
questions.answer: Their light has spread and people have come to know them widely.

questions.question: What sweet thing will a person miss if he or she looks carelessly?
questions.answer: The joy of hearing the verses’ miraculous beauty.

questions.question: What comes right after this passage to teach more?
questions.answer: A comparison about one of the highest levels of the Qur’an’s miraculousness.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the work of the Qur’an’s verses in the world?
questions.answer: They shine like stars and bring people from darkness to light.

questions.question: What kind of darkness is especially mentioned?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: What kind of light is especially mentioned?
questions.answer: The light of miraculousness and guidance.

questions.question: Before hearing the verses, how do the creatures seem in people’s minds?
questions.answer: Like dead or sleeping things.

questions.question: After hearing the verses, what do those creatures begin to do?
questions.answer: They seem to wake up and mention Allah’s names.

questions.question: What does the sky seem like in the picture made by the passage?
questions.answer: It seems like a mouth.

questions.question: What do the stars seem like in that same picture?
questions.answer: They seem like bright, wise, truthful words.

questions.question: What do all animals and plants seem like?
questions.answer: They seem like words of glorification.

questions.question: Why does the passage ask readers to imagine the old dark time first?
questions.answer: So they can better understand how powerful the verses were when they first came.

questions.question: What mistake can happen when people are too familiar with the verses?
questions.answer: They may stop seeing how amazing and powerful they are.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person will not truly appreciate if looking too shallowly?
questions.answer: How each verse removed darkness and how beautiful its miraculous recitation is.

questions.question: What does the passage promise to explain next?
questions.answer: An example showing a very high level of the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the Qur’an’s verses at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: They are compared to shining stars.

questions.question: What do these star-like verses spread?
questions.answer: The light of guidance and miraculousness.

questions.question: What do they scatter away?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: What sort of world are we told to picture before the verses are heard?
questions.answer: A world covered by ignorance, heedlessness, and a lifeless view of things.

questions.question: What happens to the world in the minds of listeners when the verses are heard?
questions.answer: It seems alive, awake, and full of praise for Allah.

questions.question: What are the stars compared to after this change?
questions.answer: To lights and words that tell truth and wisdom.

questions.question: What are the land and sea compared to?
questions.answer: To tongues.

questions.question: What are plants and animals compared to?
questions.answer: To words that glorify Allah.

questions.question: Why is it not enough to look at the verses only from our own time?
questions.answer: Because then we may miss how much darkness they first removed.

questions.question: What does being overly familiar with the verses do to a person’s understanding?
questions.answer: It can cover their beauty and make the person see less deeply.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is sweet about these verses?
questions.answer: Hearing their miraculous beauty.

questions.question: What should someone do to understand one of the highest degrees of this miraculousness?
questions.answer: Listen carefully to the comparison that comes next.
